summary: Security deep-dive focused on SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning setup, RBAC/least-privilege model, and audit log / KMS requirements for a MedScale production deployment. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send SAML/SCIM docs and RBAC matrix; customer to share admin account list and retention requirements; schedule POC kickoff.
transcript:
00:00:03 - Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - im maya patel, AE on the account, and jon from our infra security team will run through the nitty gritty.
00:00:12 - Laura (Customer): Thanks Maya, we wanted to confirm SAML setup and make sure we can do scim provisioning for groups, and importantly least-privileged roles for our teams, we also have strict audit retention needs.
00:00:28 - Jon (Redwood SE): Great. quick agenda: SAML metadata exchange, SCIM attribute mapping and group sync cadence, RBAC model (admin/editor/viewer/service accounts), audit logs retention and SIEM export, and KMS/customer-managed keys.
00:00:45 - Marco (Customer): we use Okta as our IdP, okta org: medscale-prod, and we'd like auto-provisioning via SCIM so developers get access automatically when added to groups.
00:00:57 - Jon: Okta is a common path; we support SAML 2.0 for login and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. for SAML we'll need your IdP metadata (entityID, x509 cert, SSO URL) and we'll provide the SP metadata.
00:01:10 - Nina (Customer): quick question on SCIM: do you support group sync only, or can we do attribute-based provisioning?
00:01:17 - Jon: we do basic group sync and attribute mappings. attribute-based provisioning is supported but can be flaky depending on IdP rules, so we usually recommend group-based mapping for least surprise. we'll share a mapping matrix.
00:01:32 - Maya: one thing to flag: for enterprise accounts we offer SSO with SAML + SCIM and you can opt for delegated auth in a private deployment; is that something you plan for?
00:01:42 - Laura: we prefer hosted but with VPC and customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest, if possible.
00:01:50 - Jon: CMK via KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated; for hosted we offer an option for CMEK in select regions (we'll confirm region availability). envelope encryption + HSM-backed KMS are options too.
00:02:05 - Marco: about RBAC, we need least-privilege: developers should not be able to change model rollouts or billing settings. only a small admin group can. can you walk through your role model?
00:02:18 - Jon: sure - our typical roles: Owner/Admin, Editor/Deploy, Viewer/ReadOnly, ServiceAccount (machine). Admins can manage SSO config and billing, Editors can deploy models and configure routes but not change billing or account-wide SSO, Viewers can see dashboards and logs. We'll map IdP groups to these roles via SCIM group mapping.
00:02:38 - Nina: how do you handle service accounts and key rotation? we need short-lived tokens ideally.
00:02:44 - Jon: service accounts support API keys that can be rotated; we recommend using short TTLs and automation. for private deployments we can integrate with your Vault/KMS for secrets.
00:02:58 - Maya: on audit logs, what's included and how long are they retained? also can we stream logs to our SIEM?
00:03:06 - Jon: audit logs capture auth events (SSO login, token creation), admin actions (RBAC changes, SSO config), model routing changes, and API keys usage. default retention for hosted is 90 days, enterprise plans can extend; we also support streaming logs to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS or S3 export.
00:03:26 - Laura: Audit-level detail is important for us; we may need SOC 2 evidence and an ISO attestation. do you have SOC 2 and ISO docs?
00:03:34 - Maya: yes we are SOC 2 Type II in the company, and we can share the SOC 2 report under NDA; ISO certification timeline is TBD but we can share our compliance pack.
00:03:44 - Marco: for SAML: what attributes do you require? we try to pass email, name, groups, and a custom attribute 'team' - will that map to roles?
00:03:52 - Jon: email and groups are primary. we can consume a custom 'team' attribute via SCIM or SAML assertion if you prefer to drive role assignments that way; we'll recommend mapping groups to RBAC and using attributes for fine-grained entitlements.
00:04:07 - Marco: SCIM token rotation: how often does Redwood rotate SCIM tokens? we need a process for revoking provisioning access quickly if compromised.
00:04:15 - Jon: SCIM bearer tokens can be rotated from our console; we recommend rotating every 90 days and having an incident runbook to revoke immediately. we'll include steps in the doc.
00:04:27 - Nina: data residency: our data must remain in us-east-1 or on-prem for PHI. how does Redwood support region isolation?
00:04:36 - Jon: we have region pinning for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted has region controls but not strict tenancy. for PHI workloads we recommend Private deployment inside your VPC or Dedicated with isolated GPU pool in the requested region.
00:04:50 - Laura: and encryption in transit and at rest? do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
00:04:55 - Jon: TLS for transit always. at rest we encrypt with service-managed keys by default. CMEK is available for Dedicated/Private; hosted CMEK depends on region and subscription. we'll check availability for us-east-1.
00:05:09 - Maya: on least-privilege, one implementation pattern is to create IdP groups: redwood-admins, redwood-deployers, redwood-viewers, and map them via SCIM. limit redwood-admins to 2-3 users.
00:05:20 - Marco: that fits our model. what about SSO login session length and forced reauth?
00:05:25 - Jon: session length is configurable; default is 12 hours for interactive sessions, but you can enforce shorter TTLs and require reauth via IdP sign-on policy. for API keys we recommend rotating frequently.
00:05:38 - Laura: how do you handle JIT provisioning vs full provisioning? we prefer full provisioning for predictable role assignment.
00:05:45 - Jon: SCIM full provisioning is supported; JIT is available for some auth flows but SCIM provisioning gives you better control and audit trail.
00:05:56 - Nina: on audit logs show me a sample schema, fields, and whether you include raw assertion data; also need proof of tamper-resistance.
00:06:05 - Jon: sample schema includes timestamp, actor, action, resource, outcome, IP, request_id. we can include SAML assertion IDs (not full raw assertions by default), and logs are stored with immutability controls for enterprise customers; we can discuss WORM or signed log exports for compliance.
00:06:21 - Marco: SIEM forwarding - do you push CloudTrail-style events to our S3 bucket or into Splunk?
00:06:27 - Jon: both; we can deliver to S3 in JSON newline-delimited, or integrate with Splunk/Datadog/Sumologic via HTTP collectors.
00:06:36 - Laura: vendor lock-in question: if we ever leave, can we export users/roles and logs?
00:06:41 - Maya: yes; we provide export tooling for user mappings, SCIM delta logs, and audit logs for the retention period. for long-term retention we can arrange exports to your S3.
00:06:52 - Marco: any gotchas on attribute mapping? we want group names to match our existing naming convention, not be forced into Redwood naming.
00:06:59 - Jon: we support custom group name mappings in the SCIM mapping sheet. we'll include examples.
00:07:06 - Nina: can we have RBAC rules that block certain users from invoking high-cost models?
00:07:12 - Jon: yes, RBAC can be enforced per-route/model; you can set per-role allowances or deny-lists to prevent access to specific models or endpoints.
00:07:21 - Maya: quick note on audits - we'll attach our SOC 2 summary and the redacted report under NDA; also include our support for SAML/SCIM and RBAC docs.
00:07:30 - Laura: ok thanks, that will help our security review. next, can you confirm if Redwood supports SCIM delta sync frequency and conflict resolution?
00:07:38 - Jon: delta syncs every 5-15 minutes depending on load; conflict resolution is last-writer wins for attribute changes, and group membership deltas are applied atomically. we'll document that nuance.
00:07:52 - Marco: for POCs, we want to run an auth+provisioning test and then exercise audit exports - how long to stand up a trial with SCIM+SAML?
00:08:01 - Jon: we can enable SAML + SCIM on a trial within 24-48 hours once metadata and a SCIM bearer token are provided. POC can run for 2 weeks by default.
00:08:12 - Nina: any penetration test reports? we need a pen test summary for the security team.
00:08:18 - Maya: we can share a redacted pentest summary and our security whitepaper. full reports require an NDA.
00:08:26 - Laura: great. wrap up please with action items.
00:08:30 - Maya: recap: we'll send SAML SP metadata and quickstart, jon will send SCIM mapping and group examples, customer to send list of admins/service accounts and retention targets. schedule POC kickoff - suggest 2025-12-10.
00:08:43 - Marco: sounds good.
00:08:45 - Nina: thanks all.
00:08:47 - Jon: i'll include sample audit log JSON and SIEM integration steps in the follow-up.
00:08:52 - Maya: i'll follow up with SOC 2 sharing process and the SSO docs. thanks everyone.
00:08:58 - Laura: thank you, bye.
